title: townhall-and-sprint-priorities-decision-log-v0-1
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact decision log for next sprint prioritization, a lightweight set of company-level OKR drafts for leadership review, and a tight town‑hall (company-wide) agenda and comms plan. Goal: get alignment quickly, surface tradeoffs, and leave room for engineering-level sequencing.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We have three company-scale bets for the next two quarters: 1) Make hosted API performance materially better for production customers (reduce 99th percentile latency and improve throughput efficiency); 2) Expand private deployment availability and compliance posture for enterprise sales; 3) Reduce cost per productive token with targeted batching, KV cache improvements, and a quantization roadmap. The proposed OKRs below prioritize measurable customer outcomes and revenue enablement. The townhall will be framed around these bets and concrete leader-level asks.

Proposed company OKRs (draft) - H2 2026:
Objective A — Production performance as a product (what customers feel):
- KR A1: Reduce 99th percentile token generation latency on Redwood Hosted for top 10 customer routes by 20%.
- KR A2: Achieve 99.95% availability across hosted inference endpoints (monthly SLO measure).
- KR A3: Publish three public benchmark cases (search, chat, retrieval+generate) with reproducible configs and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Objective B — Enterprise readiness and private expansion:
- KR B1: Deliver Redwood Private GA in EU and APAC regions (private control plane + KMS integration) and onboard 2 pilot enterprise customers.
- KR B2: Complete SOC2 Type II re‑audit and one targeted vertical compliance checklist (healthcare PII handling guidance + audit docs).
- KR B3: Integrate per-request audit logging into Private and Dedicated by EOY with ingestion to Console.

Objective C — Unit economics and platform efficiency:
- KR C1: Reduce average cost per 1M tokens served by 18% (mix of model routing, batching, and quantization).
- KR C2: Implement automatic prefix/KV caching for top 5 customer templates and measure 30% token reduction for those flows.
- KR C3: Build optimizer runbook that suggests model/quantization per workload; pilot with 3 internal customers.

Objective D — Developer experience & trust (grow usage and retention):
- KR D1: Increase returning API clients (90-day retention) by 15% via SDK improvements and onboarding flows.
- KR D2: Ship streaming + function-calling SDK improvements with 2 language SDKs fully instrumented for tracing and errors.
- KR D3: Publish a public reliability dashboard and incident postmortem digest cadence.

How these map to leadership asks (short):
- Eng serving/runtime: commit to a prioritized latency sprint for top 3 latency hotspots; instrument region fallback metrics.
- Product/Console: surface per-route cost/latency in the billing page for beta customers; coordinate benchmark publishing.
- Sales/CS: identify 4 enterprise customers for Private pilot and prepare data ingestion checklist.
- Research/Applied ML: deliver a quantization playbook and one pilot model quantized and validated on fidelity tests.

Town Hall (company-wide) draft agenda — 60 minutes total:
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome + state of the company (CEO, 5m)
- 0:05–0:15 — Key metrics snapshot (revenue, usage, latency, SLOs) — CFO/Head of Infra, 10m
- 0:15–0:30 — Strategic bets and OKR preview (CTO + Head of Product), 15m
- 0:30–0:40 — Customer story + Private pilot ask (Customer Success lead), 10m
- 0:40–0:50 — What to expect in next sprint (eng leads): latency sprint, caching rollout, compliance milestones, 10m
- 0:50–0:58 — Open Q&A (moderated Slack poll + live), 8m
- 0:58–1:00 — Closing ask and immediate next steps (CEO), 2m

Pre-townhall communications plan (timeline):
- T‑10 days: Leadership pre-brief and survey to gather 3 cross-team questions (owners: Priya + Alyssa).
- T‑7 days: Publish short 2‑page preview (one-pager) + short video (3m) describing the 3 bets to all employees. Include a 2-question pulse survey (support/concern).
- T‑2 days: Reminder with specific product demos links and how to submit questions.
- T+1 day: Post-townhall recap + decisions and actions doc with owners.

Decision log (entries) — lightweight, append-only:
- 2026-02-16 | Decision: Prioritize latency sprint over new SDK features for two sprints. Owner: Marco Rivera. Rationale: latency regressions reported in three paying customers; short-term revenue risk.
- 2026-02-20 | Decision: Run Private EU pilot with AcmeHealth and NFinTech. Owner: Samir Patel. Rationale: both need regional KMS and audit logs for procurement.
- 2026-03-04 | Decision: Delay publication of public benchmark until dedicated rollout handling is in place. Owner: Dana Lee. Rationale: benchmarks must reflect stable routing policies to be meaningful.

Sprint prioritization summary (current two sprints):
- Sprint A (next 2 weeks): latency hotspot fixes, tracing & 99th percentile dashboards, critical cache implementation prototype.
- Sprint B (following 2 weeks): KV cache rollout for top templates, Private EU KMS integration work, quantization pilot integration test.

Risks and mitigations (top 5):
- Risk: Overcommitting engineering capacity and missing SLA promises. Mitigation: freeze non-essential feature work, hire temporary contractor support for SDK docs, communicate realistic timelines.
- Risk: Benchmarks create customer expectations we cannot commit to. Mitigation: frame benchmarks as reproducible configs with disclaimers; involve product in messaging.
- Risk: Compliance scope creep for Private pilot. Mitigation: define Minimal Viable Audit (MVA) checklist and lock scope for pilot customers.
- Risk: Cost optimizations impact model fidelity. Mitigation: run fidelity regressions against curated prompt sets and gating for any automatic quantization rollout.
- Risk: Townhall content too exec-focused, low engagement. Mitigation: include two short customer stories and one live demo; collect questions ahead of time.

Open questions for leadership discussion (need quick decisions):
1) What is the acceptable floor for model fidelity when applying automatic quantization? (proposed: 98% on our eval suite)
2) Are we committing to firm Public Benchmark publishing date or moving to rolling publish?
3) How many additional headcount FTEs can Product/CS have to support enterprise Private pilots this quarter?

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Priya: finalize townhall one-pager and send pre-brief by 2026-03-12.
- Marco: publish latency dashboard draft and 99th percentile measurement plan by 2026-03-17.
- Samir: confirm Private pilot contracts and MVA checklist by 2026-03-24.
- Alyssa: prepare comms video script and coordinate internal demo by 2026-03-18.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally concise; please comment inline in Drive with "accept", "adjust", or "escalate" tags for each OKR line.
- We want leadership alignment by 2026-03-20 to allow teams to schedule sprints for the first two-week window.

Appendix (short):
- Measuring friction: suggested metrics for adoption and trust: returning API clients (90-day), average token latency P50/P90/P99, Dedicated capacity utilization, Private pilot onboarding time (days), and Number of fidelity regressions after quantization.
- Link references: Confluence:COMPANY-STRAT-2026 (roadmap), Jira ENG-1421 (latency infra epic).

End of doc.
